validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/ENDPOINTS/DUPLICATE, all confirmed independently of gem.wiki. This is PNGRB-authorised regulation-21(1) 'Tie-in Connectivity' asset 21.01.NGPL 'Jaigarh - Dabhol', entity code WCPL, authorised 18.05.2015 - present, unchanged, in every PNGRB NGPL MIS Report edition I pulled and pdftotext'd myself (Feb-2023 'as on 31.12.2022', Jun-2024, Mar-2025, Jun-2025, Dec-2025). Independently, offshore-technology.com's project page for H-Energy's Jaigarh terminal describes the same 60km tie-in, PNGRB-authorised May 2015, EPC by Engineers India, connecting the Jaigarh LNG Terminal to GAIL's Dahej-Uran-Panvel-Dabhol and Dabhol-Bangalore transmission networks at Dabhol - matching GEM's StartLocation/EndLocation and confirming PipelineType=transmission (it is a high-pressure tie-in into the national transmission grid, not a gathering/feeder line). Times of India corroborates the Jaigarh LNG Terminal itself (H-Energy's FSRU-based terminal, inaugurated May 2018) as the pipeline's origin point. Fuel=Gas is trivially correct (LNG regasified to pipeline-quality natural gas). DUPLICATE CHECK: the 35-pipeline roster has no other Jaigarh-origin row. gem.wiki separately documents a 'Jaigarh-Mangalore Gas Pipeline' (H-Energy Gateway, 635km, 17 MMSCMD) - but that is a genuinely distinct, CANCELLED project (PNGRB revoked its authorisation 4 July 2022) on an entirely different corridor (south toward Mangalore, not the short Dabhol tie-in), so it is not a duplicate of P0930 and needs no action. CAVEAT: the PNGRB report format changed between the Dec-2025 and May-2026 (current) editions - the entire itemised 'Tie-in connectivity' table (which held this row plus ~8 unrelated ONGC/GAIL tie-ins) was dropped from the report, and the WCPL entity abbreviation disappeared from the legend along with it, while HEPL (H-Energy Private Limited) was left in the legend unused. Read this as a report restructuring (tie-in mileage is now folded into aggregate totals only), not evidence this specific pipeline was deauthorised - the row was stable and unchanged for the ~3 years of editions before the format change.

validity.researcher_notes: SPEC (length/capacity) confirmed at high tier. PNGRB's NGPL MIS Report lists the Jaigarh-Dabhol (WCPL) row with Authorised Length 60.00 km and Authorised/Design Capacity 29.00 MMSCMD, verbatim and unchanged across every edition I checked from Feb-2023 through Dec-2025 (I fetched the PDFs directly and read them with pdftotext -layout, since url_verifier's text-extraction check gives a false negative on these large PDFs per this batch's documented gotcha - I confirmed 200 status live via the verifier and confirmed the actual numbers by hand). This is an EXACT match to GEM's LengthKnown=60.00/CapacityUnits=MMSCMD/Capacity=29.00. Independently, offshore-technology.com's trade-press project page corroborates the PNGRB authorisation and the 60km figure. Minor non-issue: several 2018-2022-era press pieces (offshore-energy.biz, nsenergybusiness.com) describe the tie-in as '56 km' or '57 km' - PNGRB's own Operating-Length column shows why: only 56.37 of the 60.00 authorised km were built/in-service as of the Dec-2022 snapshot, reaching the full 60.00/60.00 km by the Jun-2024 snapshot. So the '56-57km' figures are contemporaneous construction-progress snapshots, not a disagreement with GEM's final as-built 60.00km - no correction needed.

validity.researcher_notes: OWNER confirmed at high tier. PNGRB's entity-code legend spells out 'WCPL = Western Concessions Private Limited' in every edition of the NGPL MIS Report I checked, matching the 21.01.NGPL Jaigarh-Dabhol row's entity code exactly - this matches GEM's Owner1='Western Concessions Private Ltd' at 100% precisely. Independently, Oil & Gas Journal's coverage of H-Energy's Hoegh FSRU charter names 'Western Concessions Private Ltd.' by name as the H-Energy project subsidiary tied to this pipeline. Two independent origins (regulator + trade press) agree on the exact legal name - no change needed.

validity.researcher_notes: STATUS/START-YEAR plausibility concern, not an existence concern - the pipe itself is real and PNGRB-confirmed mechanically complete (see the spec entry above). The problem is that this is a DEDICATED single-purpose tie-in whose only intended gas source is the Jaigarh LNG import terminal, and that terminal's own history makes GEM's StartYear1=2021 look wrong and the unqualified 'operating' status worth re-checking: (1) the terminal's FSRU (its only regas unit, Hoegh Giant) did not even arrive at Jaigarh until 1 March 2022 - a year AFTER the terminal's originally-announced 'March 2021' commissioning target (nsenergybusiness.com project page) - so no LNG could plausibly have reached this pipeline as early as 2021; (2) Hoegh LNG terminated the FSRU charter in April 2022 over 'the charterer's default of the contractual terms' and withdrew the vessel from India entirely (two independent LNG Prime articles, both verified live); (3) I found no report of a permanent replacement FSRU having entered service since; (4) ownership of the whole Jaigarh terminal project changed hands from H-Energy to AG&P Pratham around December 2024 (constructionworld.in, verified live), and as recently as the AG&P negotiation coverage (offshore-technology.com, verified live) the terminal is still described as a stake being acquired/negotiated, not as an operating asset. So for essentially the entire period since this pipe reached its full 60km (PNGRB shows that by mid-2024), its sole supply source has had no working FSRU. GEM's StartYear1=2021 reads like the terminal's originally-ANNOUNCED target year carried over onto the pipeline, rather than an actual first-gas date - a recognized failure mode (dating an asset from an announcement instead of an outcome). I could not independently confirm actual gas throughput either way (PNGRB's tie-in table does not publish the gas-supplied/capacity-utilisation columns that its main common-carrier tables do), so I'm flagging rather than proposing a specific corrected value - Delayed=yes/DelayType=confirmed IS well supported by this same evidence and needs no change.

summary: Existence/classification/endpoints/length(60km)/capacity(29 MMSCMD)/owner(Western Concessions Private Ltd) all confirmed high-tier via PNGRB (WCPL, 6 editions Feb2023-Dec2025) + trade press, independent of gem.wiki; STATUS CONCERN flagged - StartYear1=2021 looks like the terminal's originally-announced target rather than actual first gas, since the pipeline's sole LNG source (Jaigarh FSRU terminal) didn't get its FSRU until Mar-2022, lost it to contract termination Apr-2022, and changed owners (H-Energy to AG&P Pratham, Dec-2024) without a confirmed replacement since - 'operating' status is plausible (pipe is mechanically complete) but unverified for actual throughput; no UNRESOLVED refs, Diameter left blank (no line-specific source found).
